summary:
I'm approving: every prior finding is fixed and the delta adds no defect.

(1) Batch starvation is fixed. The outer select in round() now filters `o.kind IN (:known)`, built from Kind.values(). The NOT EXISTS subquery still runs over all kinds, so an unknown row still holds back newer rows of its own aggregate but no longer takes a batch slot. Kind.valueOf in the row mapper is now safe because of the filter. The new test puts BATCH+1 BOGUS rows on separate aggregates ahead of one valid row and asserts that row is DONE. It would have failed before the fix, because the 101 older unknown rows filled the LIMIT 100 batch. An @AfterEach removes the BOGUS rows from the shared database.

(2) Logging is fixed. reportUnknown() logs one ERROR per pass with the count and a sample of at most 5 id:kind values. Both queries hit the PENDING-only partial indexes. `uuid || ':' || kind` resolves through anynonarray||text, and both relay tests exercise it.

(3) AC-9b wallet cases are added and correct. walletDebitBreakerOpen: a 5000 balance means the wallet pays all 998, so the method becomes WALLET; walletDebit then throws the open breaker, unwind and reverseWalletDebitDurable run, and the test asserts CANCELLED, RESTORE_STOCK and exactly one REVERSE_DEBIT row. paymentCreateBreakerOpenAfterPartialWalletDebit: with a 300 balance against 998, the method stays CARD; createPayment then throws the open breaker, unwind runs with wallet=true, and the test asserts CANCELLED and a CREDIT row of 300.00. Both use the real OrderRemote and WalletCreditBacks, so the durable rows and the error translation are real.

(4) The racer test now fails on its own assertion. It calls couponAndPartialWalletAvailable(), and @BeforeEach already stubs reserveStock and createPayment. If the guard were removed, both racers would place orders and return null instead of DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE, so the assertion fails rather than an incidental NPE.

(5) AC-8 now has placement-level fail-fast tests for inventory, promotion and payment. Inventory and payment assert CANCELLED with exactly one order row; promotion asserts zero order rows, since coupon validation runs before the save.

(6) Both nits are fixed: the dead `fingerprint() != null` checks are gone, and CodedException and ErrorCode are imported.

The engineer's diagnosis of the earlier AC-8 failures is right. With no encoder set, Feign's builder uses Encoder.Default, which only handles String and byte[]. It throws EncodeException for a record body before the client runs, so the breaker never saw those calls and never opened. Production is not affected. DependencyBreakerConfig registers the capability as a bean, so OpenFeign applies it to every client, with its usual Jackson-based encoder. DependencyBreakerCapability.execute wraps the Client and does not look at the HTTP method: it records any IOException or RuntimeException, and any response with status 500 or above, as a failure. So production does count POST 5xx and I/O errors.

Widening the time bound from 1 s to 2 s is fine. It is still under the 3 s read timeout, so a timeout wait would still fail the test, and the assertion that the stub host received no calls is the main proof anyway.
